sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Orca is a desktop workspace for running AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. You can run several agents in parallel worktrees, review their diffs, and ask bots in Slack, Linear or GitHub to fix bugs and open pull requests.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running coding agents in plain terminals gets messy once several tasks run at once, and agents stop when you step away. Orca gives each task its own workspace, lets agents keep running on remote machines, and pings you on your phone when one needs you.
whoFor: Developers running Claude Code, Codex or other CLI agents
Teams that want bots fixing issues from Slack, Linear or GitHub
People who run agents on remote servers or cloud VMs
Reviewers who want to annotate AI-written diffs
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you work with several CLI agents at once and want one app to run, review and steer them. It uses your own agent subscriptions and machines rather than its own model.
requirements: At least one CLI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor and others)
Optional: the iOS or Android app for notifications

overview: Orca works with any agent that runs in a terminal, including Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Goose and many more. You can use an agent in a chat UI or as its raw CLI and move a conversation between the two.

Tasks can be split into parallel worktrees so agents don't interfere. An orchestrating agent can start worker agents in their own workspaces and bring results back. Orca Bots respond to requests in Slack, Linear or GitHub and return tested pull requests, running on your own Claude Code or Codex.

Agents can run on a remote Orca server, any SSH host, or a cloud VM, so they keep going when your laptop sleeps. Built-in review tools let you comment on exact changed lines, draft commits and PRs, and send failing checks back to an agent. A mobile app notifies you when an agent needs input.
